title: Japan offers idle oil tanks for Philippines-led stockpiling plan
summary: Japan is offering its unused oil storage tanks to support a Philippine-led regional stockpiling program.

blocks.text: Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi (L) looks at Philippines' President Ferdinand Marcos Jr during the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on Nov. 17, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — Japan has offered to make its unused oil storage tanks available for a Philippine-led regional stockpiling program, as Asian countries seek to build emergency fuel reserves against future supply disruptions.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced the proposal Tuesday, Nov. 17, at the Asia Zero Emission Community Summit in Manila, where leaders discussed the region's energy security as supply challenges mounted due to Middle East conflict.
The proposed arrangement would allow participating countries to use spare storage capacity in Japan as part of a joint effort to secure oil supplies during emergencies.
Takaichi also called for stronger cooperation under the Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience Asia, a framework launched in April 2026.
The initiative seeks to strengthen the region's energy resilience alongside its longer-term transition toward carbon neutrality.
Japan's stockpiling offer forms part of broader proposals at the summit, including the creation of an Asia Oil Security Task Force.
Envisioned as an Asian counterpart to the International Energy Agency, the proposed task force would coordinate oil procurement, stockpiling and emergency releases during major supply disruptions.
The framework would have a coordination hub in Tokyo, Japan.

Another proposal, Bridge Asia, seeks to promote joint research and development among participating countries in emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, digital technology and quantum computing.
The initiatives reflect efforts to strengthen regional economic and energy resilience alongside existing commitments to reduce carbon emissions.
Separately, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin signed a memorandum of understanding with the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia on Sunday, November 15.
The agreement provides a framework for technical cooperation and policy support aimed at strengthening Philippine energy security and advancing the country's energy transition.
The Department of Energy is targeting at least 25 gigawatts of renewable energy capacity by 2035 as part of efforts to expand the country's clean energy supply.
